To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vicious circle between poverty and environmental degradation can be broken by means of an entrepreneurial approach that involves stakeholders’ integration.
“The key to breaking the “vicious circle”, is for firms to develop entrepreneurial strategies that integrate the needs of vulnerable communities and that are adaptable to the changing environment”.

“the vicious circle between poverty and environmental vulnerability can be broken by a collaborative effort between firms and communities that is based on stakeholder integration, entrepreneurship and a holistic framework for intervention”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a framework for the analysis and evaluation of strategies and scenarios to promote sustainable development in vulnerable areas.
the development of strategies and policies which can help firms and communities to break the vicious circle between poverty and environmental vulnerability.
the following question: How can firms and communities collaborate to develop innovative solutions which can break the vicious circle between poverty and environmental degradation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework is useful for the design of interventions in order to break the vicious circle between poverty and environmental degradation.

firms should collaborate with local stakeholders in order to develop entrepreneurial strategies that are able to break the vicious circle between poverty and environmental degradation, and that such collaboration should take into consideration the specific context in which the business intervention will occur.
firms should collaborate with local communities in order to develop and implement innovative strategies that will improve the environmental conditions of the local communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a holistic framework which integrates the concepts of vulnerability, entrepreneurship, and stakeholders’ integration, in order to provide a better understanding of the complex interplay between business and environment.

the business intervention should be based on a holistic framework that integrates three main dimensions: adaptability (the ability of a community to adapt its business activities to changing circumstances), entrepreneurship (the ability of communities to develop new business opportunities), and stakeholders’ integration (the ability of firms and communities to work together to improve their business activities).

the integration of stakeholders in business interventions, the development of entrepreneurial capabilities and the adoption of a systemic and holistic perspective can contribute to the improvement of the welfare of vulnerable people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
business intervention strategies should aim at promoting entrepreneurship, stakeholder integration and adaptability.
the most effective strategies are those which are based on the adaptation and entrepreneurship of both firms and communities.
firms and communities should be able to adapt to changing environmental conditions in order to break the vicious circle and to develop a sustainable development model.
